summary: Backend regression of floor-layout upload pipeline through new storage abstraction (LocalStorage). 15/15 pytest tests passed against the live preview backend (Couchbase Capella) covering happy-path upload, byte-perfect round-trip, all 3 validation rejections (content-type/extension/size), 404 on bad floor_id, admin-only enforcement on POST/DELETE, GET /api/uploads auth + 404 + path-traversal + disallowed-extension, JPEG content-type variant, and full upload-then-delete cycle (DB field cleared + object removed + previous URL 404s).

minor.issue: Content-type sniffing is purely client-supplied (file.content_type startswith 'image/') — a hostile client can still upload arbitrary bytes labelled image/png with a .png extension. Consider validating with magic-bytes (Pillow/imghdr) for defense in depth.

Size check happens after the entire payload is buffered into memory via await file.read(). For 10MB+ rejected uploads the pod still allocates the buffer; consider streaming/chunked size check or rely on starlette max_request_size.

On delete we sniff every allowed extension (png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp) and call storage.exists()+delete() per ext. With OBSStorage that's up to 5 HEAD calls per delete — would be cheaper to persist the actual filename/key on the floor record at upload time.

Sanitization strips '..' chars but the regex `[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]` already removes '/', so `../etc/passwd` becomes `..etcpasswd` — the explicit `'..' in safe_name` check then rejects it. Logic is sound but a comment would help future maintainers.

action_items: Optional hardening: validate uploaded image with magic bytes in addition to client content-type.
Optional perf: store the exact storage key on the floor record so DELETE doesn't probe all extensions (matters for OBS).
Consider returning 413 explicitly (instead of 400) for oversized uploads to align with HTTP semantics.
critical_code_review_comments: buildings.py upload_floor_layout: content-type validation only checks startswith('image/') from the client header — server should also verify magic bytes for OBS deployments where uploads are public-readable.

DELETE handler iterates ALLOWED_IMAGE_EXTENSIONS and calls storage.exists()+delete() for each — fine for LocalStorage (cheap stat) but on OBS this is N round-trips per delete. Persist the storage key on the floor doc at upload time.
storage/__init__.py get_storage() is a process-global singleton — STORAGE_TYPE env changes after first call require process restart (documented behaviour, just worth noting).

LocalStorage.put writes synchronously via open(...).write() inside an async route handler — small files only so it's fine in practice, but technically blocks the event loop. aiofiles would be cleaner.
seed_data_creation: Each test creates a throwaway building (TEST_storage_* / TEST_delete_*) with 1 floor and deletes it in fixture teardown. No residual data should remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Storage refactor is solid for LocalStorage backend. OBSStorage path was NOT exercised live (no OBS endpoint in preview). If OBS deployment is later tested, set STORAGE_TYPE=obs + OBS_* env vars and re-run /app/backend/tests/test_floor_layout_storage.py — same 15 tests should pass against OBS.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. All listed features behave as specified.
